business_model.claim: Match Group sells digital social-connection and dating services through a portfolio of consumer app brands, including Tinder, Hinge, Match, Pairs and Azar.
quotes: Our global portfolio of brands includes Tinder®, Hinge®, Match®, Meetic®, OkCupid®, Pairs™, Plenty Of Fish®, Azar®, BLK®, and more, each built to increase our users’ likelihood of connecting with others.

business_model.claim: Most brands use a freemium model: the service is free to use, and a subset of users pays for premium features.
quotes: Most of our brands monetize via a freemium model where the use of the service is free and a subset of the users pay for subscriptions or in-app purchases to access premium features.

business_model.claim: Direct revenue comes mainly from recurring subscriptions sold to end users, and to a lesser extent from one-off à la carte feature purchases.
quotes: Our direct revenue is primarily derived from users in the form of recurring subscriptions, which typically provide unlimited access to a package of features for a specified period of time, and to a lesser extent from à la carte features, where users pay a non-recurring fee for a specific consumable benefit or feature.

business_model.claim: Advertising (Indirect Revenue) is a small share of revenue: in Q3 2026 Direct Revenue was 876,624 and Indirect Revenue was 14,608, out of Total Revenue of $891,232 (table in thousands).
quotes: In addition to direct revenue from our users, we generate indirect revenue from advertising, which comprises a much smaller percentage of our overall revenue as compared to direct revenue.

business_model.claim: Subscription fees are paid in advance and recognized straight-line over the subscription term, so the balance sheet carries deferred revenue of 151,929 at September 30, 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: Fees collected, or contractually due, in advance for subscriptions are deferred and recognized as revenue using the straight-line method over the term of the applicable subscription period, which primarily ranges from one week to six months, and corresponding in-app purchase fees incurred on such transactions, if any, are deferred and expensed over the same period.

business_model.claim: The company now reports three operating segments: Tinder, Hinge and Everyone Everywhere. Everyone Everywhere combines the former Evergreen & Emerging and MG Asia segments.
quotes: During the quarter ended June 30, 2026, we reorganized our brands into three operating segments.
Specifically, the Evergreen and Emerging and MG Asia operating segments were combined into a new segment called “Everyone Everywhere.”

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by the number of Payers and by Revenue Per Payer (RPP). In Q3 2026 total Payers were 13,789 against 14,527 a year earlier, and total RPP was $21.19 against $20.58.
quotes: Revenue Per Payer (“RPP”) is the average monthly revenue earned from a Payer and is Direct Revenue for a period divided by the Payers in the period, further divided by the number of months in the period.

business_model.claim: Tinder is the largest segment, with Q3 2026 Direct Revenue of $480,019 (table in thousands). That revenue declined 2% as Payers fell 4%, partly offset by a 2% rise in RPP.
quotes: Tinder Direct Revenue declined 2%, driven by a 4% decrease in Payers, partially offset by an increase in RPP of 2%.

business_model.claim: Hinge Q3 2026 Direct Revenue was $220,586 (table in thousands), up 19%. The growth came from 23% Payer growth tied to European expansion, partly offset by a 3% decline in RPP to $31.81.
quotes: Hinge Direct Revenue grew 19%, driven by 23% Payer growth, reflecting Hinge’s continued European expansion, partially offset by a decrease in RPP of 3% to $31.81 as a result of the expansion of discount optimizations and testing of a new lower priced subscription tier.

business_model.claim: Everyone Everywhere Q3 2026 Direct Revenue was $176,019 (table in thousands), down 20%. The decline includes a $20 million drop at Azar and Payer declines at most brands in the segment.
quotes: E&E Direct Revenue declined 20%, including a $20 million decrease in revenue at Azar resulting from the changes discussed in the Azar business update above.

business_model.claim: App-store policy can move revenue directly. Apple's removal and later redesign requirement for Azar lowered monetization, and in 2025 76% of Azar's $155.8 million Direct Revenue came through Apple's App Store.
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025, Azar Direct Revenue was $155.8 million, of which 76% was through Apple’s App Store.
The app updates necessitated by the new guidelines resulted in lower monetization from the new app.

business_model.claim: Distribution depends heavily on Apple and Google, through which the mobile apps are almost exclusively accessed.
quotes: Additionally, our mobile applications are almost exclusively accessed through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

business_model.claim: The main cost of revenue is in-app purchase fees paid to Apple and Google, generally up to 30% on iOS and 15% on Android for subscribers. These fees totalled $687.1 million in 2025.
quotes: a meaningful share (for subscribers, generally up to 30% on iOS and 15% on Android) of the revenue we receive from these transactions
Total in-app purchase fees were $687.1 million and $696.6 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Moving Payers to alternative payment methods cut Q3 2026 cost of revenue to $206,522 from $247,043 (table in thousands). The shift produced $43.0 million lower in-app purchase fees, partly offset by $4.5 million higher card processing fees.
quotes: Cost of revenue decreased across all segments primarily due to Payers shifting from app store payments to alternate payment methods, resulting in $43.0 million lower in-app purchase fees partially offset by an increase of $4.5 million in credit card processing fees.

business_model.claim: Google fee terms are a cost driver: the Google partnership entered into in 2024 expires in the first quarter of 2027.
quotes: In particular, our partnership with Google entered into in 2024 is set to expire in the first quarter of 2027.

business_model.claim: User acquisition marketing is a major cost. Selling and marketing expense rose to 185,028 in Q3 2026 from 169,142 (table in thousands), and higher marketing at Tinder and Hinge is cited for the expected Q4 Adjusted EBITDA decline.
quotes: The cost of acquiring new users has consistently been one of our larger operating expenses.
The Y/Y decline in Adjusted EBITDA is largely due to increased marketing spend at Tinder and Hinge and a gain on sale related to an LA office building in the prior year quarter.

business_model.claim: Personnel costs, including stock-based compensation, drive product development and G&A. Stock-based compensation expense was 177,354 for the nine months to September 30, 2026, against 194,167 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: Product development expense consists primarily of employee compensation expense and stock-based compensation expense that are not otherwise capitalized for personnel engaged in the design, development, testing, and enhancement of our services and related technology.
